# CASA requirement register

Source: [App Defense Alliance CASA Specification v2.1.1 (2026-06-03)](https://github.com/appdefensealliance/ASA-WG/blob/main/CASA/CASA%20Specification.md). Test procedures: [CASA Test Guide](https://github.com/appdefensealliance/ASA-WG/blob/main/CASA/CASA%20Test%20Guide.md).

Every audit item is checked on every commit by `scripts/verify.sh`:
- **verified**: the cited tests, lint rules and tools must exist and pass.
- **n/a**: if code matching a reopen pattern appears, the gate fails until the item is re-assessed.
- **pending**: work still owed. Allowed during development, but `CASA_STRICT=1` (release CI) fails.

The controls below still apply, and are tested, if they are switched on. Passwords are hashed with Argon2id (m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1, OWASP's minimum, pinned in auth/password.rs) with a 128-bit random salt per password, as a PHC string. Unknown emails still cost one verification, so timing doesn't reveal accounts. Not yet: breached-password check (ASVS 2.1.7). |

## 4 Communications

| ID | Requirement | Status | Evidence / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.1 | TLS is enforced for all connections (TLS 1.2+, secure cipher suites) | ✅ verified | `tool:check-tls`<br>`tool:zap-baseline`<br>`file:nginx/default.conf.template`<br>`lint:insecure-transport`<br>`test:redirect_uri_must_be_https_fixed_and_exact`<br>`test:every_response_carries_security_headers`<br>`file:docker-compose.prod.yml`<br>nginx terminates TLS 1.2/1.3 only with forward-secret AEAD suites (Mozilla intermediate), no session tickets. Port 80 only answers 301 to https://hadalspace.com (the fixed canonical host, never the request's Host) for Hadal's own names, plus the ACME challenge; unknown host names get no response, and on 443 an unknown SNI name is refused before any certificate is sent. HSTS (2 years in the image; 5 minutes in local compose so localhost isn't pinned) is sent exactly once on every response, including the proxied API. scripts/check-tls.sh checks all of this against the running stack in CI (refuses TLS 1.0/1.1 and non-FS/CBC suites), and ZAP scans over HTTPS. The OAuth redirect URI must be https except on localhost. Production (docker-compose.prod.yml) serves hadalspace.com with a Let's Encrypt certificate renewed by certbot; port 80 serves only the ACME challenge and the redirect. Before the assessment, run check-tls.sh against hadalspace.com and attach an SSL Labs report. |
| 4.1.2 | Connections to and from the server use trusted TLS certificates | ✅ verified | `tool:check-tls`<br>`test:remote_database_requires_verified_tls`<br>`test:production_client_refuses_plain_http`<br>`lint:tls-verification-disabled`<br>Backend to Postgres: TLS with sslmode=verify-full against a private CA (certificate and host name 'db' checked); the backend refuses to start with a non-local DATABASE_URL that isn't verify-full. Postgres requires TLS 1.2+ for every network connection (pg_hba hostssl only, hostnossl rejected); check-tls.sh confirms every live connection is TLS and a plaintext one is refused. Backend to Google: rustls, Mozilla roots, https only. nginx to backend is plain HTTP inside the private compose network, which never leaves the host. For a managed database use its CA as sslrootcert. |
| 4.1.3 | No weak cryptography affecting confidential data | ✅ verified | `lint:weak-crypto`<br>`lint:insecure-randomness`<br>`tool:semgrep`<br>`test:round_trips_and_uses_a_fresh_nonce_each_time`<br>Refresh tokens and imported mail (summary, body, attachment names/types/sizes, and the user's Gmail label names) are encrypted with AES-256-GCM (ring) under DATA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, with a random 96-bit nonce from the OS CSPRNG per value. Attachment files are not stored: they are fetched from Gmail when downloaded. |
| 4.1.4 | Cryptographic modules fail securely; no padding oracles | ✅ verified | `tool:check-tls`<br>`file:nginx/default.conf.template`<br>`test:hashes_are_salted_argon2id_and_verify`<br>`test:tampering_wrong_row_or_wrong_key_fails_closed`<br>TLS is the only encryption, and nginx allows only AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) on TLS 1.2 plus TLS 1.3, so there are no CBC suites to build a padding oracle on; check-tls.sh confirms CBC and non-forward-secret suites are refused. At rest, the app encrypts Google refresh tokens and imported mail with AES-256-GCM from ring (backend/src/crypto.rs): authenticated encryption with no CBC and no padding, so there is no padding oracle. A wrong key, wrong associated data (another row), tampering or truncation is an error, and no partial plaintext is returned. Otherwise the app hashes (SHA-256 for tokens, Argon2id for passwords), and Argon2 verification fails closed (a malformed hash is a mismatch). rustls (backend to Google and Postgres) has no CBC suites. |

## 5 Data Validation and Sanitization

| ID | Requirement | Status | Evidence / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.1.1 | Protect against HTTP parameter pollution | ✅ verified | `test:duplicate_json_keys_are_rejected`<br>`lint:raw-query-string` |
| 5.1.2 | URL redirects and forwards are limited to allowlisted URLs | ✅ verified | `lint:open-redirect`<br>`tool:check-tls`<br>`file:nginx/default.conf.template`<br>Every redirect has a fixed target. Backend: only through auth::redirect(), to Google's authorization endpoint (an AuthorizeUrl only GoogleClient can build) or constant same-origin paths; nothing comes from the request. nginx: HTTP->HTTPS redirects go to CANONICAL_HOST (hadalspace.com in production), never the request's Host header. Requests for any other host name hit default servers that close the connection (port 80), refuse the TLS handshake for an unknown SNI name, or answer 421 when the Host header differs from the SNI name, so the edge can't be used as an open redirect or serve the app under someone else's name. check-tls.sh checks this on the running stack in CI. |
| 5.1.3 | No eval() or other dynamic code execution | ✅ verified | `lint:dynamic-code`<br>`tool:semgrep` |
| 5.1.4 | Protect against template injection | ➖ n/a | No server-side templating. The UI is compiled SolidJS JSX, which escapes text by default. |
| 5.1.5 | Prevent server-side request forgery | ✅ verified | `lint:outbound-http`<br>`test:production_client_refuses_plain_http`<br>`test:gmail_ids_are_checked_before_use_in_a_url`<br>All outbound HTTP is in backend/src/auth/google.rs, to Google's constant endpoints: token (code exchange and refresh), revoke, and the Gmail API under https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/ (message list, messages, and message attachments). No host or URL comes from user input; Gmail message IDs from Google are checked to be plain alphanumeric, and attachment IDs plain base64url, before they go into a path segment; the only labels ever sent as a list filter are our fixed system-label constants or user label IDs Gmail itself returned from users.labels.list, re-checked against a strict pattern before use. User label names and colours from Gmail are cleaned and validated before they are stored. Responses are size-capped (attachments at Gmail's 25 MB limit). Redirects and proxies are disabled on the client; lint:outbound-http rejects HTTP clients anywhere else. |
| 5.1.6 | Protect against XPath or XML injection | ➖ n/a | No XML is parsed or produced. |
| 5.1.7 | Context-aware output escaping protects against reflected, stored and DOM XSS | ✅ verified | `lint:raw-html-sink`<br>`lint:tabnabbing`<br>`test:every_response_carries_security_headers`<br>`file:nginx/security-headers.conf`<br>`tool:semgrep`<br>`test:html_only_bodies_become_text_with_scripts_and_styles_dropped`<br>`test:attachments_download_as_files_never_inline`<br>`test:download_names_cannot_break_the_header`<br>API: JSON only, nosniff, CSP default-src 'none', set by the backend alone (nginx adds no headers to proxied /api/ responses). UI: Solid escapes interpolations, raw HTML sinks are banned, strict CSP from nginx. Imported mail is never rendered as HTML: HTML-only bodies are reduced to plain text on the server, and the UI shows bodies as text in a <pre>. Attachments are only ever downloads: always application/octet-stream with Content-Disposition: attachment (whatever type the email claims), under the API's nosniff and CSP, so a file from an email can't run as a page on our origin. File names are cleaned at import and encoded in the header so they can't inject parameters. |
| 5.1.8 | Protect against database injection | ✅ verified | `lint:sql-string-building`<br>`tool:semgrep`<br>All SQL is static text with sqlx bind parameters. |
| 5.1.9 | Protect against OS command injection | ✅ verified | `lint:os-command` |
| 5.1.10 | Protect against local and remote file inclusion | ✅ verified | `lint:filesystem-access`<br>`lint:directory-listing` |
| 5.2.1 | Uploads are limited to expected types and never executed | ➖ n/a | No file upload functionality. |
